Fire Pulse.

NASA Space Apps 2026 · Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots

A burning-activity calendar for Australia, 2023–2025. VIIRS detections are rescaled to the MODIS baseline so the satellite record can be read as one consistent series.

1 · Choose a region

Drag a box on the map, or pick a preset.

Each square is 0.5° (about 50 km), shaded by total harmonised detections 2023–2025.

2 · Burning calendar

–

–

One square per day. All three views share one colour scale, so the raw VIIRS view shows how much hotter the record looks without harmonisation.

3 · Fire season timing

When each year's burning started, peaked and ended in this region, so crews can plan for the critical period.

Start, midpoint and end are the dates by which 10%, 50% and 90% of the calendar year's harmonised activity had happened. Southern regions whose season spans December–February are better read from the calendar.

4 · Is this year unusual?

One year against the range of all years, week by week.

5 · Weekly activity: raw vs harmonised

When the harmonised line sits on the MODIS line, the conversion works. Raw VIIRS shows the gap that harmonisation closes.

Busiest weeks

    Monthly activity (harmonised detections)

    High: at least 1.5× the month's 3-year average. Low: at most half of it. With the full 2003–present archive this becomes a 20-year baseline.

    8 · Which forecast was right? 2026 test and 2027 outlook

    Six algorithms predicted 2026 using only 2023–2025. Their predictions were locked before any 2026 data was seen, then scored against real NASA MODIS detections for January–October 2026. The winner forecasts 2027.

    9 · Method and validation

    –

    1. Clean. Keep vegetation fires (type 0): MODIS confidence ≥ 30, VIIRS confidence nominal or high.
    2. Grid. Count detections per 0.5° square per day, separately for each sensor. A detection is a fire pixel, not a whole fire.
    3. Calibrate. Learn how many MODIS detections match one VIIRS detection, per square, pulled toward the national factor where a square has little data.
    4. Machine learning. A gradient-boosting model (scikit-learn, Poisson loss) predicts each square-day's MODIS count from VIIRS detections, fire power, day/night split, confidence, season, location and the square's k.
    5. Validate. Learn on 2023–2024, test on 2025, a year the models never saw. Both methods are scored the same way.
    K = ΣMODIS ÷ ΣVIIRS
    kcell = (Mcell + λ·K) ÷ (Vcell + λ), λ = 200
    Ratio method: Harmonised = VIIRS × kcell
    ML method: Harmonised = f(VIIRS features), learned

    2025 test (never seen during calibration)

    Stability: K by year, day and night
